GitHub: @SahajIVVIX-1 Enterprise Agentic RAG Orchestrator is a production-grade Multi-Agent Agentic RAG system designed for complex enterprise workflows.

Supervisor→Worker→Validator pipeline routes every query to the right specialist agent, with a LangGraph-powered Corrective RAG loop for high-fidelity retrieval and a strict human-in-the-loop protocol for external actions.

Supervisor-Worker-Validator architecture utilizing LangGraph and LangChain to route queries among specialized agents (Corrective RAG, Natural Language to SQL, Human-in-the-Loop external tools, and Conversational agents).

angGraph : Implemented a self-correcting retrieval graph that uses an LLM grader to evaluate document relevance, dynamically triggering query rewriting and re-retrieval (bounded to 2 iterations to prevent latency spikes).

OpenEnv Data Cleaning Environment An OpenEnv environment where an agent cleans a dirty pandas table one action at a time, plus baselines, a benchmark, an LLM agent and a Gradio demo.
- Reproducible: every episode is (task id, seed) - the same dirty table, with a hidden clean ground truth.
- Honest scoring: the training-style reward and the final grader score are separate things (see below).
- Agents included: do-nothing, random, a rule-based heuristic, a trained RL agent (PPO), and a zero-shot LLM agent (Llama 3.
The RL agent is trained with PPO on held-out seeds and runs via lightweight pure-NumPy inference with zero PyTorch dependencies at runtime.
The Hugging Face Space demo runs at chetangadhiya017-data-cleaning-env.
To redeploy the latest code, see Deploy.

Reward Q is an observable quality score: Q = 1 - (schema violations + duplicate rows n columns) / (initial rows n columns) .
The progress terms add up to 10 (Q end - Q start) , so repeating actions or going in circles cannot earn reward (there is a test for this).

Deep DCGAN Reproducibility Study: Architecture & Analytics A research-centric implementation of the DCGAN paper (Radford et al.
, 2015), modernized with 2018-2022 stability techniques and a professional post-training analytics pipeline.
🚀 The Vision This project isn't just about training another GAN—it's about understanding it.
While most implementations just show you a grid of fuzzy images, this study dives deep into the "black box" of the Generator and Discriminator to visualize exactly how latent vectors become features.
Key Highlights Modern Stability : Upgraded the 2015 baseline with LSGAN (Least Squares) and Spectral Normalization to prevent the dreaded "vanishing gradient" problem.
Deep Diagnostics : A custom GANAnalyzer class that hooks into the model's internal layers to visualize learned filters and feature maps without needing to retrain.
High-Fidelity Evaluation : Automated 4-panel dashboarding for immediate assessments of model convergence and Nash Equilibrium.
Modern Implementation A formal comparison between the baseline architecture proposed by Radford et al.
(2015) and this enhanced, high-stability version for facial/object generation.

Executive Summary While this project replicates the All-Convolutional architecture and upsampling strategy defined in the 2015 paper, it adopts several modern training paradigms discovered between 2017 and 2020.
These enhancements collectively solve the "instability" and "mode collapse" issues inherent in the original BCE-based GANs.
Mathematical and Architectural Comparison Component Radford et al.
06434) My Implementation (2026) Technical Rationale : : : : Loss Function Binary Cross Entropy (BCE) Least Squares GAN (LSGAN) BCE suffers from vanishing gradients when the D is too strong.
LSGAN (Mean Squared Error) forces the G to generate data closer to the decision boundary even when it's already "passing.

Normalization Batch Normalization Spectral Normalization Spectral Norm enforces a Lipschitz constant of 1, providing a mathematical guarantee against the Discriminator's gradients exploding—crucial for high-res stability.
02) Modern Xavier/Kaiming Hybrid Faster convergence and better flow of gradients through deep strided convolutions.
3) Prevents the Discriminator from "overfitting" on the real dataset, which often causes the Generator to fail mid-training.
9] Softens the target for the Discriminator to prevent it from becoming "too confident," which helps maintain gradient flow for the Generator.
Analytical Core (The "Research" Layer) The original paper relied heavily on simple grid visualizations.
This implementation introduces a dedicated GANAnalyzer framework that mirrors paper's Figure 5 but expands it with professional metrics.
Fig 5: Filter Visualization Original Paper : Visualized 128 randomized filters of the G's projection layer.
This Project : Extracts and plots the RGB-channel filters of the first D layer, showing exactly what edge/texture detectors the model learned during the 25-epoch CIFAR-10 run.

Modern Dashboards (Not in Paper) Precision-Recall Histograms : Overlapping probability distributions ($D(x)$ vs $D(G(z))$) are used here to detect Mode Collapse before it happens—a diagnostic tool not available in 2015.
Feature Map Hooks : We use PyTorch hooks to visualize the "intent" of the generator in mid-layer (e.
, at 16x16 resolution), providing a peek into how a low-dim latent vector becomes a high-dim image.
Conclusions for Reproducers If we were to strictly follow the 1511.
06434 paper, we would likely encounter the "jittering" loss common in early GAN research.
By replacing the loss function with LSGAN and adding Spectral Normalization, we have successfully modernized the 2015 architecture to perform with 2026 levels of stability and detail.
Reality The original 2015 DCGAN was ground-breaking but famously unstable.
This repository serves as a Reproducibility+ study.
I've kept the original "All-Convolutional" architecture but swapped the underlying "engine" for something more robust.
I’ve documented every architectural shift from the 2015 paper to this implementation.
Check out the Deep Paper Comparison for the full breakdown of why these changes were made.
